What an amazing concept for a game!
I played through the entire  game, and I was very impressed with the story. It kept me wanting to find out more links between the characters.  The only reason I was disappointed is because the game ended. I wanted more story!  more time in game!!

***If you liked the book "1984", then you will love this game***

Overall:  10/10

Amazing game, short.. but nontheless worth the money you spend on it. Coupled with several different endings, different branching paths, this game is nothing less than a masterpiece that i will remember for quite a while. Excited for the next game!
After one playtrough, I can definitely recommend this game. I'd like to see this turned into a movie, somehow.

A thought provoking game that teaches you about the potential risks  when you aren't careful of what you say on the internet. It could of used some more video content to show events like in the beginning of the first episode.

This game really made me think about privacy issues in real life. I can only recommend this game if you have patience, love stories that makes you question the world around you and like reading a lot.

Def one of the most unique and enjoyable game experiences i have had in a long time. Especially great to unwind to after work and before you know it youre totally engrossed in the game. 
Orson Wells was a badass
10/10
Fun game with an intresting story line, but rather short. Has some reply value to get other outcomes and acheivements.

'Orwell' will die Spieler geradezu polarisieren. Das Spiel selbst sieht aus wie ein Browser und lässt sich gleich bedienen. Das Gameplay ist also wie das tägliche Internetsurfen und womöglich sogar Arbeiten. Es handelt dann auch noch über die totale Überwachung durch das Internet der Dinge. Welche Auswirkungen das hat, kann man noch gar nicht wirklich vorhersehen. Die Osmotic Studios zeichnen eine dystopische Geschichte im Stile von '1984' vor und zeigen dem Spieler die positiven und negativen Konsequenzen dieser Überwachung. Dazu betten sie das Spiel noch in aktuelle Themen ein: ein Terroranschlag in der hiesigen Stadt. Zusammen mit der spannenden, wendungsreichen Geschichte zeigt sich ein individuelles Spielerlebnis, das durch die Spielerentscheidungen sehr deutlich von anderen Spielern abweichen kann. Geleitet wird das ganze durch die Grundeinstellung der Spieler. Ist man gegen oder für Überwachung? Sieht man eher die Vorzüge oder die Nachteile der Überwachung? Lässt man Verbrecher lieber laufen, oder nutzt das System? 'Orwell' schaffte es mich ein wenig zum Nachdenken zu bringen, denn der relativ neutrale Zugang zum Thema ist sehr selten. Ein wunderbares Erlebnis, das nahezu uneingeschränkt zu empfehlen ist!

I picked this game up when the first two episodes released, and let me tell you, getting the notification that Orwell needed my attention every time the next episode came out was simultaneously thrilling and disquieting. I desperately wanted to see how things were about to unravel! I was also increasingly anxious about the fates of everyone involved. The pacing on those episode releases was spectacular, and I don't think I've ever played an episodic release schedule I enjoyed more.

It's all out now, obviously, but I don't think that will detract from the experience one bit.

Very strongly recommended. And now I'm taking a break to think about my life and my choices before I venture in to ruin lives in altogether different ways in a splinter reality.

Orwell is a great game. It sets in the world of Big Brother aka the government. Your sitting there gathering data of unsuspecting users happily posting all their life story on social media. In reality now it makes you think should I really post that on (insert social media)? Yep. The NSA is watching everyone possible.

Small indie game with a great concept and an amazing story.

Definitely worth a pickup at 10€.
I played through the whole thing in a bit over four hours and was absolutely *riveted*. Great way to tell a story and it really makes you think. Now I want to see the other outcomes....

fantastic game for a very reasonable price. I would highly recomend everyone at least check out the demo. 
Gives you a very interesting view on surveillance these days.

Orwell is one of those games that makes you think. It makes you think about how surveillance works in the real world. It makes you think about what you put online as this can be misunderstood or taken out of context. It makes you think about what your credit card statement says about you. Most of all though it makes you think about what is considered as right and wrong.

Orwell is a game where you play a person sat at a computer terminal extracting information from the internet about people to stop a series of terrorist bombings. Through what information you decide to pass on to your handler and which conflicting statements you believe the game will pan out very differently. How relevant is it that somebody doesn’t like to go out and party? Not very much on the surface, but what if they later say they are going out clubbing all night? Seems unusual for somebody who actively dislikes this, doesn’t it? Are you reading too much into this? Or is this information going to stop a bombing? Orwell constantly asks you to reassess your understanding of the characters you are investigating. One phone call or chat message could convince you that they are a terrorist or vice versa and you need to just weather the consequences.

For the full review please visit [url]https://bitsandpieces.games/2017/03/02/orwell-review/[/url]
This game is amazing. I am a huge fan of George Orwell's 1984 and when I found this game I thought "I hope It lives up to the book" and my god it did!

Somewhat linear, but it doesn't make it less fun. The story and implications in themselves make it well worth the (short) time you'll spend on it. Some replayability (for achievements).
Kind of makes you think about what you should (or shouldn't, rather) post on the Internet.
Interesting concept
I can finally prosecute people without reason :')
Great game, lets you deicide fate and has great dialogue. Makes you more aware about your online presence.

Hoooo boy. How to start.

Orwell is absolutely Orwellian, but for any literature nerds like me out there, this isn't like an adaptation of 1984 or Animal Farm or even Homage to Catalonia. But The Nation, the central society that the game takes place in, is an Orwellian state. Someone's always watching. In this case, it's you. An act of terror has been committed, and it's up to you to sift through blogs, emails, telephone calls, texts, photos, even remote-accessing citizen's computers in order to find out whodunnit. Esentially, you ARE Big Brother. Similarly to Papers, Please, you work for the system. But that's where the similarities stop because Orwell is visually stunning, with an intuitive interface and in-your-face consequences for your actions.

I've played every dystopian, utopian, cyberpunk, post-cyberpunk, pre-cyberpunk, and anything that even sounds like cyberpunk game I could get my hands on, and this is easily in the top five percent. Orwell allows you the freedom to choose what kind of observer/reporter you'll be. Will you try your best to do what's right by the Nation? Will you use your position on the inside to help the resistance? The choices can be subtle - I found myself making honest mistakes, people going to prison who didn't deserve it or worse. And what's equally intriguing as what's in Orwell is what is implied - the type of society you're observing, her inhabitants. There's a lot of reading, but it establishes a base for a complex and interesting world. If I had to fault it, it would be on replayability. You're allowed to explore so much and the resolution is so memorable that I can't imagine being as surprised again. Even so, I immensely enjoyed my playthrough.

Orwell was worth every cent I paid for it. In fact, it's one of the best games I've played this year. It was beautiful, engaging, and timely. You won't regret playing it.

For the Steam awards I nominated this for the "Just 5 More Minutes" award. I sat there last night at 9pm, just after getting home from work, and then didn't detach from the screen until 2am. I had many a time in the game said that I would process a lead, and then logoff Orwell, and then just kept going, and going, and going...
Really great game. Lots of unexpected story twist, amazing music and great use of sound effects for the atmoshpere.
A great marriage of theme and gameplay.  Not especially challenging, but manages to be fascinating from beginning to end.
A great game, very thought provoking. Makes you realise just how much personal information is available from the most innocent sources!

Great game! I love how the game gives you all the information needed to uncover the case, but also gives you superfluous or downright false information to give you a chance to be wrong. Your choices and actions really matter in this game, and it proves the ineffectiveness of this extent of government surveillance.

When I saw a game named Orwell, I just knew I had to play it.

Orwell is a fantastic, stark look at a very big brother type of government can monitor and control its population.

You play as an investigator looking into an increasingly complex terrorist plot against the fictional nation. At your disposal is the Orwell system, capable of looking into the complete digital lives of your suspects and finding their intermost secrets in an attempt to stop them.

All the while, it makes you think whether or not what you are doing is the right thing, and how much control is too much control.

It is a game that gives you questions. Questions that challenge you and your opinions. And that is great!

If you want a game that is deep, questioning but also fun and satisfying at the same time, them you need to get this game
I play a lot of game where I could be ''evil'' but I never feel bad about it... Until I played this game.. You learn how easy it is to lose your humanity

When I read the name of this game my interest was piqued.

There's a lot to like about Orwell. Putting the player in an active role of the "Überwachungsstaat" (surveillance state) was a great move. On the one hand, it felt good to save lifes, but on the other hand I had a lot of power over people's life and caused suffering of innocent people, only because I misinterpreted a piece of information.

I have a feeling that I'm gonna play this game at least once more, just to see how different the story turns out.

Engaging and making you think. Quite a lot.
Very well done. Well constructed complex personalities and stories. Nothing is obvious in here.
Simple yet powerfull interaction.

This game.. It's an experience unlike any other I've had. Comparable to the first time I read 1984, but instead of reading about a story that takes place, you're put into the shoes of an "investigator" using a twisted surveillance system that has access to just about everything. Phonecalls, internett history, private pictures. Question is, what will you do with these powers, and who's watching you?

If dystopian novels and unique games without 4k demons or dragons sounds like your thing, take this one for a ride.
Great game!

All I can say about this game is wow!

Set in a very near, and highly plausible future, you are recruited to take part in a security program called Orwell. While seemingly a good idea on paper, Orwell may or may not translate well in the real world.

A great and thought provoking game about state surveillance, paranoia, terrorism, social media, media bias, etc. Osmotic Studios have created a very immersive game that will not disappoint.

TL;DR -> Fantastic game, just don't put this "datachunk" in my Orwell profile... ;)

When I first saw this game, I thought it was going to be an interesting, and appropo examination of modern politics. What I got was an emotional journey that made me care... perhaps a bit too much? The line this game walks between the modern day and the dystopian future is subtle and slim - the characters are appropriately real, even visceral.

Everything about this game is simple and elegant, exactly as a good social network should be. It's comfortable and familiar, yet alien and disturbing, given the game's story. This game is a great example of design being part of the story.

The branching choices may not be especially robust, but they give a lot of replay value. Their purpose is to bring the full weight of that moral burden to bear on your soul, and that's exactly what this game excels at. It makes you think, ache, and puzzle along with these characters. It makes you root for them and against them.

The only negative thing I have to say is that when I got stuck, I got very stuck. And towards the end of the game, with so many pages available, it was hard to get back on track and find where I was supposed to look. It would be helpful if entire pages, and not just data chunks, would disappear when they became useless.

This game was recently nominated for a Game Awards, and it totally deserves it. If you want to play a thought-provoking, choice-based game that's also well-designed, this is for you.
It is a pretty solid game, even though it is very short.

BEST USE OF A FARM ANIMAL ~ Steam Awards 2016

Basically this is NSA Simulator. It's an amazing game, but horiffying to think about the fact that this kind of stuff goes down in real life.

All in all though, it's an amazing game and a riveting story.
Great game. Characters feel real. Would incriminate again.

This is seriously the favorite game in my library. If I had to choose one game that would stay in my library, this is an easy pick.

But onto more generalized viewpoints,
Even if you don't think your choices matter as much as they possibly could, like in a Telltale game, there are fixed events, but that isn't a bad thing, necessarily. But your choices do matter. Some people could get arrested, some people not. You can make someone look worse than they are. Take things out of context. It's your choice, really.
But Orwell is about the story. The story has tons of "wtf how" moments. It thrills you, it saddens you.
On the art form, it's great. Of course it isn't realistic, it isn't cartoony. It has a low-poly style, but it still has tons of detail.

Really, I don't want to spoil it. Just play it.
A game in a dystopian future where your every move is monitered hats off to the creator for the plot twist at the end. now that it is fully released it's a must play.

Orwell is a fascinating game that explores the ethical considerations of a government software system that scrapes the Internet for data on people. Is it a bit linear? Maybe. But I didn't find the plot twists predictable, and it has enough replayability that it's definitely worth your time if the concept intrigues you. This is a rare occasion where I paid full price for a game, and still felt that I got my money's worth. Definitely recommended.

This game is both beautiful and terrifying.

Here's the skinny:
- It's a short game
- It has a few different endings
- If I were a teacher, I would make this "required reading"

The game is basically a look at what mass surveillance would be like from an investigator's point of view. I don't want to say too much more than that.

Gameplay is pretty simple: drag-and-drop different pieces of information to make progress on a case that revolves around an explosion. The story is delivered through text via a contact that talks to you directly, and also via snooping around in people's personal lives.

Do you like George Orwell's 1984, or perhaps the TV show Person of Interest? You'll probably dig this game.

Big brother is out there, and you are the eyes!!

I absolutely loved this game. Episode 1 seemed somewhat short, but episodes 3 and 4 certainly made up for it. I predict if you play this game, and follow the story, unless you are VERY vigilent you will not guess "whodunit".

It is also very interesting to replay and sway the course of the game by your actions, or in-actions. The choices you make really do have an effect, though obviously there will be a narrow range of main endings for any of these games, but the details will change.

Orwell is a fun and unique game. You play as a government agent tasked with investigating a terrorist attack, it is your job to act as a gatekeeper between the personal information of those under investigation, and the agency that will act on your information. Through this role you can filter out incorrect information (or pass it on), color your employer's perceptions of those under investigation, and ultimately, play a hand in their fate. The game has you make multiple choices that affect the outcome of future episodes, and decide what endings will be available to you. Don't let the demo fool you, it doesn't stay linear for long. One playthrough is fairly short(~4-5 hours for me), but it has some good replay value if you make different choices the second, third, or fourth time around.

Orwell is a story-based experience, along the same vein as Papers, Please. You play as a citizen, recruited by a country called The Nation, to help spy on their citizens for possible criminal activities. You use a program, called Orwell, to spy on people's emails, phone calls, computers, or anything else that may help you in your investigation.

You submit information to Orwell, called Datachunks, which can help or hinder your investigation - some are useless and others are very useful bits of info. The gameplay consists of you scouring though social media feeds and other information to try and find suspects involved in a bombing - then submitting those datachunks to Orwell where a 3rd person, named Symes, interprets your findings. Because of this nature, it's possible many things you submit will be out of context and Symes may think the information more dangerous or important than it appears.

In short, Orwell is an intruging experience where the player is constantly questioning the validity of such a spying system and as a player you have to make some important choices indeed. Do you withhold information because these people are not dangerous at all? Perhaps you submit faulty information to get Orwell off the trail? Or do you be a good citizen and help The Nation find these terrorists?

I'd recommend Orwell for those looking for a rich story experience. If you liked Papers, Please or Telltale games, this should definitely be up your alley.

Bought this on a whim and found it really addictive. The whole idea of prying on peoples private lives legally within the seems morally wrong but objectifably correct in the context of the game. There are twists and turns and every step meaning you never quite know what will happen next. This is also effected by the evidence you compile over the game. Finally, it is perfectly named as this has several shadows of 1984 and Animal Farm with the whole 'Big Brother' idea imprinted in the entire game.

Really worth buying if your interested in something a little different form the usual gaming fare plus you can try the first chapter for nothing!

This game (or visual novel, rather) definitely has a rather small demographic. I think most individuals will /know/ whether they'll like this game from the get-go based solely on its theming, so if you're into that hacker-esque, Orwellian, mass-surveillance type thing, you honestly can't go wrong picking this up and playing through it.

BIG BROTHER IS WATCHING. 

* this game has a deeper impact after few episodes of Black Mirror * 
* and maybe pay some respect to old George Orwell's 1984 to feel the vibe * 
* some red wine would be nice too * 

We all make decisions - sometimes to save lives, sometimes to create chaos. And rarely we make them as distant observers , but not in Orwell. Prepare yourself to dig someone's dirty laundry, check on their "not_so_facebook" timelines, listen to their calls and... well, feel the spirit of being a stalker for a good cause! 
Or perhaps not so good - it will be your decision after all. 

This journey doesn't require walking through pixel woods or shooting into some birds in the sky. Your castle is a database. 
Your axe is your data-chunks, so drag them wisely, we don't want wrong heads to roll, right? Oh, and no princess (or prince) to save! But still some moral choices will await you. 

Anyways, 9.5/10. I enjoyed every minute (even those when I screwed up).
A brilliant and intelligent game, confronting you with the issues of mass surveilance. One of the best games released this year!
It's an interesting little game. I'm not sure it will appeal to everyone, but I'd encourage anyone who enjoys a strong story based game to at least try episode one for free.

This one flew under my radar but as soon as I found it, I knew I'd love it. Part George Orwell, part super computer, ORWELL puts you sort of in charge of watching people. Always watching. Though sometimes the controls can feel a little awkward, and your brain might fly faster than you can click through things, Orwell gave me the heebie-jeebies. 

It might leave you feeling a little confused, and you might come away from it wondering if this is the future (for better or worse), but it's worth the time.

Not my kind of game: I have only played 29 minutes, maybe it gets more interesting later on.
It has very low resolution, you need to drag some text items from stories on the right hand of the screen to the left of the screen where it is added to dossier and by doing so the dossier gets more detailled. Basically all you have to do is scroll trough some text stories and move the highlighted parts. Repeat.
A novel concept for a game and really a bit disturbing how much data the "investigator" was willing to upload.

I absolutely love this game and would recommend it to anyone who likes dystopic visions, top-notch storytelling, and has light voyeuristic tendencies.

Playing a secret agent who listens to 'normal' citizen's phone calls, reads their chats, follows their social profiles, and generally checks the digital world for clues if those citizens might be criminals is exciting and disturbing at the same time.

The unique graphics only underline this strange atmosphere that fits all too well in our time. I don't want to spoil too much, so if all this sounds good to you, jump right into it!
One of the diamonds of 2016 gaming. Cool, interesting, intence. Would recomend to people who like stories in games.

Absolutely amazing. Have been completely unable to tear myself away from this game for the last four hours. Fascinating story, open-ended choice-making. Fans of Papers,Please and Hate+, this is a must-play. You owe it to yourself to play this take on the visual=novel-esque genre..

YAY DOXXING SIMULATOR 2017 
MAXIMUM SPERG EDITION!

Orwell had me lost for words. Featuring a variety of references to George Orwell's dystopian political and surveillance novel, the game offered an interesting concept as to what may have been the beginning of Oceania. Of course this game has no canon with the novel that I happened to study in school just before discovering this game.

There is something extremely captivating about playing a game in which you dig into the most private aspects of the lives of several different characters. From the start, I was sure that there would be some revelation that you should not enter information that may harm the futures of these potentially dangerous characters but the actual plot twist featured at the end of the game was both unexpected and in a way poetic.

This game surpassed my expectations and with a beautiful soundtrack and imagery featured through-out this Papers, Please reminiscent game was captivating and extremely fun. I highly recommend it.

Notes: I played the first episode/demo for free before purchasing the game and playing all but one episode in one night (I would have played the final episode but I had to go to sleep for work the following morning).

An expertly crafted indie game that gives an altered perspective on government spying and national security.
As it's name inplies, this game deals with the moral qualms of surveillance on a national scale. The player is dropped into an investigation team of a new spying system called Orwell. The gameplay is easy to grasp and there is little to none when it comes to a learning curve. Just drag and drop information of people who are to be suspected and thats about it. There is a beauty in its simplicity. The story unravels and presents twists and turns that will make even the strongest uneasy. Some information that's gathered may also conflict other possible information, that is were the players decision making comes into play. All this is given a backdrop of a subtle and ambient soundtrack. The only con I have is that the minimalistic style and story is not enough and there isn't the ability to replay previous episodes for a different turnout. However, it is a great delivery of a dev team of like 3 people. Definitely a must play at $10 and for those who are technologically inclined or interested in the aspects of surveillance.

I've enjoyed having a game that isn't like every other game.  It reminds me a bit of a recent mail-order solve a mystery in a box puzzle I played, only with feedback and stress.  I enjoy the open ended nature of the game and the freedom you have to influence the outcome - highly recommend.

I'm always looking for a great new game to play and Orwell fit that mold really well. The story is very captivating which is accentuated by the music and characters in the game. I really enjoyed the twist at the end and the multiple choices it offers. I really recommend this game if you're looking for something different and captivating.
A bit sort but lots of fun. Hope to see some new stories soon.

I give this game 8/10. Really fun game right up until the ending.  The game stresses choices and the repercussions of said choices but in the end you are simply given your choice of ending. None of your choices really mattered, it was all a sham. I really really enjoyed episodes 1-4 of the game, but the ending left a bad taste in my mouth.
Thumbs up.

This game is phenomenal. From the art to the general interface. 
1. This is not an adrenaline game
2. This game is 50/50 on Story to Game Play
3. This game is not for everyone- this game is for people that like the experience and the art of a good story.

And...

4. This game will make the conspiracy theorists, anti-gov, and generally anxious yell "SEE! THE WORLD IS OUT TO GET ME!"

A true masterpiece of the video game industry, this game expertly weaves intuitive, albeit slightly reduced, gameplay and relevant social commentary, which is them wrapped up by a contemporary take on 1984's version of Big Brother.
This game made me feel guilty about how much fun stalking people online turned to be.

I finished the game in a little over 17 hours. It seems short, but I really liked the story and it was very immersive. I do think there are other games out there with more replayability for a better price but yeah. The one thing that bothered me about Orwell is I could not skip through videos/text I've already seen. My play time would have been a lot shorter if I had been able to do that. I liked the way they told the story, being able to be in control of the data recieved is really cool and an interesting way to do a "whodunit". On my first playthrough I was shocked with who the real culprit was until around Chapter 4. In my next playthrough I was able to see the links and things that I had missed, since I now knew who the culprit is. The entire time I played it my fiance was glued to the screen watching me play and asking questions about what he had missed, and questions he had. If this seems interesting to you, I'd recommend buying it. If you're hesitant just wait for a steam sale and check it out.
Absolutely fantastic game so far, really poignant at the moment as well, at least in the UK with the Snooper's Charter.

It's a very engaging game that really requires you to *think*, but even then when you consider all the options it, think you've got it figured out, it can still shock or at least surprise you! Very good, and definitely worth replaying at least once or twice after you finish it once, if only to see if you can actually nail the criminal.

At the end of it, though, you really are left thinking considering the rights and wrongs of the solution presented. :)

One of the best games I have found in recent times. Fantastic story, really engrossing and a great look at the other side of the Big Brother style narrative, making the ethics behind the 1984 like overbearing government more based upon your own.  I would recommend this game for the full price, so if you ever see it on offer, snap it up!

Top game
Make choices that change things

Picked the game up in the first place beacause ist seemd like a novel gameplay experience and it definity delivered.

Also its so easy to get drawn into the role as an investigator and very easy to overlock the fact that you are shamlesly shifting through other peoples lives.

also this is probably the first game where i had the feeling that the episodic release really worked.

So I got this game because I read and absolutely [i]loved[/i] 1984. There's plenty of references to the novel that are absolutely wonderful, but that's besides the point.

Orwell is a "Big Brother" simulator- You play the role of "Big Brother" as a cog in a mighty Orwellian machine. You prevent a couple of crimes, possibly get someone killed, the usual Big Brother stuff. Then you fall foul of a hacker who's learned about the machine (Aptly named "Orwell") from a source known as "W1n5t0n". This happens around Episode 3. This hacker is a threat, and leaks data on a government employee, leading them to become the head target for Orwell... Until the activist group they're part of catches wind of you. There's three possible endings which I won't delve into too much, but suffice it to say that one of them lets you become Edward Snowden. That's the one I picked.

this game is all about monitoring stuff, sometimes you can get stuck on a level, but there are subtle hints everywhere, and thats why i like it.
the developers made a detective game that isnt just shoving hints into your face, and you cant use "give me a clue and make the game meaningless" skill.
overall, a really great detective game, and a superb story.

8/10

I wasnlt sure if I would enjoy this, but after playing the demo (which I was very appreciative of) I thought I would give it a try. I liked the story and there is a high replay value to do things differently, so well worth the money.

Orwell is a rather close-to-the-bone spy em' up, not dissimilar to titles like Uplink in that they are set entirely in a digital, UI-based world.
Orwell has you performing surveillance on citizens of The Nation to ameliorate and defend against terrorist threats. 
The plot is compelling and is currently made up of five episodes, which altogether will take the average player around 2 hours to complete.
Unusual in it's gameplay mechanic, Orwell asks you to collate data about subjects (or targets) from the internet; using sites similar to Twitter, Facebook and blogs, you submit information to The Nation which allows it's security service to act. 
Information found and submitted is dependant on you, the human factor - decide to omit a vital piece of information, or include a misleading fact and you will influence what happens next.
This introduces some very difficult decisions and will test your ethical code. 

Orwell is highly reccomended - George would have been proud. Probably.

This developer needs to work on more games! Right off the bat, I must give kudos where they are due. I did feel like I was spying on people, the twist ending was awesome, and the level of detail was fantastic. I particularly liked easesdropping on their conversations in the 'live' chat and email modes and picking out the gems for Orwell to classify. Great indie game!
Great game with a great plot. Doesn't matter if you try to be the good guy, or try to make everyone look guilty.

Highly Recommended. Story is well crafted, with twists that I certainly didn't see coming. The issues dealt with within the game (survelliance, privacy etc) are also very relevant to the present day. A bit on the short side and not much replayability, but still a highly enjoyable experience regardless.
I've played through this game twice, and got about 11 hours of enjoyable gaming out of it. I will play through it one more time to see if I can change the story even more. I recommend this game.

Highly highly recommended. This is the absolute best game of 2016 and highly under rated. It looks incredibly basic and easy but it is anything but. Highly immersive and addictive. Crashed once but was fixed by the time episode 5 as launched the following week and it worked fine. No ending is guaranteed and no outcome is easily predictable. There are multiple endings depending what YOU choose to do and submit to Orwell. I've spent almost 3 hours on the game at the time of writing and intend on going through it doing different things the next time and see what happens. Its highly unnerving and brilliant and the soundtrack is well worth getting as the soundtrack is one of my absolute favourites. There is literraly one stage in the game where you get hacked and I thought my actual laptop was getting hacked it was done that well. The story line is brilliant and I'm hoping there will be a sequel or second season.

Now, I do not review games. I just play and have fun, and leae it at it.
I Purchased this game out of sheer curiosity, because Orwell. And I am so glad, I did.
It is a really good game - each episode unveils a new thing about Orwell and Thought. It shows you an insight to what could happen in the future (hopefully, though, we won't get there).  I wanted to know everything about everyone in this game, and found myself enjoying this bit of spying a bit too much at times - this game allows you to get fairly deep into history of the people you follow, and it is up to you to decide what is important, what not. I also really enjoyed the art itself, and it is not something I always pay attention to. The episodes don't really feel like episodes - it is more of a feeling of a finished day at work, and each time you start a new day, you get a nice brief of everything that has been done so far. I am planning to replay the episodes again as it seems like the game can have different endings, and I am really curious as to how different they actually are.

All in all, I really enjoyed it. It is not extremely expensive, and it provided a few hours of good fun.

while Orwell isn't really about an orwellian government, but something more like an authoritarian and intrusive one, this game really stands up for its originality, narratives, and mechanics of the game.

In Orwell, we will take the role of an investigator working for the government of ''the nation'' on a new security program called Orwell, and as a result of a terrorist attack, we will be investigating on whoever has organised these attacks, and hopefully, arrest them. With orwell, you will be able to spy on them, listening to their calls, reading their messages, the e-mail, and so on.

so, what is it that you do in this game? READING. In this game 100% of the time, you'll have to read, if you don't like reading, this is not the game for you. Sometimes, you'll have to make important decisions that could lead to the success of your entire investigation or big mistakes that will affect the story and have unforseen consequences.
But this isn't a game only about investigation, it highlights the dangers of the internet, social networks, and pretty much everything that we post online, it's like a ticking bomb, waiting to be discovered one day and be used against us.

there isn't really much to talk about the technical aspect of  the game, since this is a kind of a ''desktop simulator''(wich is  really well made by the way) it has a really cool story, great characters that you get attached to, and a really good soundtrack that perfectly fits the title of this game. 

basically, if you like story-driven games, and/or are interested on the subject of mass surveillance, i would definitely recommend this game to you.

Okay first off, I just finished the game for the first time through, so I can only speak to the progression of the game through my single experience. 

What an entangled, involved, deep ride it was! All the minor and major bits of plot and character development... left me speechless. When I first got into this game, I was hopeful that it wouldn't be a flimsy investigative journalism style that left gaping holes in character development in favor of quick story progression. So with endless red herrings, conflicting information, tiny bites (bytes?) of data that all weave together, I very quickly became engrossed in finding out everything I could, and frequently found myself at odds with my own judgments and thoughts based on what the information was telling me. 

The atmosphere of the game is sober, at times haunting, and at times pulse quickening depending on what's going on. And I think that this is very much appropriate for the moral of the story. This is invasive, what the player is forced to do... to get this job done. It spends time and effort bringing the player from one side of the spectrum to the other in terms of how helpful or hurtful a surveillance system like Orwell can be. 

In the end, or at least the end of the story I found... I was left with a feeling of completion... ... and thoughtfullness. Yes it's a game, but it has a very real moral message in it, that when the end credits roll make you really consider the implications of our REAL digital lives, and how easy it is to comb through and assemble these very damning dossiers. And how dangerous that could be if the 'powers' that be decided to use it as a means of control and 'protection'. I haven't reacted to a game in this way in a long time... so it bears a review. 

Extremely well made, thought provoking, in depth, orwellian (aptly named!), driving, robust game WELL worth a play. The only drawback I can find is that some people don't like a game where they have to read a lot. And there's a TON to read, combing through all the various resources for hints and clues, and entanglements.

Orwell is a very unique experience. It puts you in the role of a beta tester for a new peice of software that allows for total monitoring of the populus. You work with an employee of the company that developed the software and look into clues via many different methods of investigation (web browser, hacking into PCs, monitoring text chats & phone calls, etc.). You get to choose which peices of information go into the report taht is sent to the company - which then makes decisions on how to react to that information - so it adds an element of choice that is intersting and most scenarios are not morally clear. Without going into too much detail on the story, the representation of your "big brother" monitoring techniques is very well done and makes you feel like you are blending the line between helping keep the country safe and violating their right to privacy. It has some pretty emotional outcomes and definately does a great job making you care about the choices / really feel the outcomes. Again, nothing quite like it. A great game to experience. The developers are continuing to update it, as well, so it is getting more free episodes as they months go on.

Really great game! Mechanically very simple but the story is interesting and everything helps the Big Brother theme. The "information without context can be dangerous" message is strangely appropriate for the current climate.

It has multiple routes through the game depending on which information you submit or ignore.

Really enjoyed the playthrough, each chapter is an hour long which felt long enough. Easily recommend.

At first I thought this game would just be reading documents and listening to conversations to report on offenders plotting to create havok in the real world...was I ever so pleased to be wrong. This game has an incredible hidden depth and replayability that amazed me as you delve deeper into the chapters.

Choices loom for each peace of information you submit to Orwell as an investigator and even the smallest peice can have devastating or positive impacts to the characters of the game. It is a simple concept of the game but genius, and creates a more immersive experience than I would have thought possible for this style of game. I definitely recommend this to others to try, it will challenge your decision-making and morals alike.
